notes: Coders agreed on all three documents being delegates (CUNY policy defers AI use to syllabi and instructors). Main disagreements on matched units: (1) P19 vs P06 for 'AI to generate content without written authorization' - resolved to P19 since the text never addresses silence; (2) phase for definitional lines (general vs when-misuse or course-start vs during-work) - definitions of misuse set to general, student duties on conforming to assignment policy set to during-work; (3) modality/stance of citation clauses (must/permit vs must-not/restrict) - set to must/permit consistently; (4) actor and type for rationale lines in the CUNY Explanation (P44 vs P56, all/admin/student) - institution-level principle set to P56/admin, student-skill rationale kept P44; (5) should vs must for a Chicago style instruction - should. Unmatched units: B-only units were all dropped as not AI-related or duplicating another unit (homework aggregator uploads, posting/orientation, prior violations, unfair-advantage rationale, level playing field, presentation offer, syllabus-defines-policies); all A-only units were kept (Hunter's review-charges duty, A's separate library sentences, Chicago citation sentence). Because Hunter pages and the library guide repeat the CUNY text, matched shares are inflated by repeated units.
